candidates.detail: Assume a character’s personal minute is StrategicMinute::MAX, one active cheap owned holding has next_due_minute MAX, no occupants, no other active due holdings, no existing receipt for that due date, and the character has exactly eight units of accepted currency. The authored base charge is four. The first loop iteration records a paid receipt and deducts four from the local available counter; saturating MAX plus the 30-day period leaves next_due_minute at MAX. The same due date is selected again, the paid receipt already exists, but another four are deducted and counted as spent. A third selection records an unpaid receipt at the same date and makes the holding dormant. After the loop, eight units are debited if currency consumption and the enclosing transaction succeed. This follows source control flow and integer arithmetic only; no product or database was run.
candidates.safeguards: The authored cheap, moderate and fancy owner and renter charges are positive, so this example is finite as funds run out; it is not an asserted infinite loop. Other holds, occupants and insufficient funds change the sequence. Acquisition and paid settlement use saturating clock arithmetic, while the core DuePeriods iterator uses checked addition and stops at overflow. Whether MAX personal time, a saturated due date and the stated state are reachable in a supported production run remains unproved. Any later transaction failure may roll back effects.
